All for daily workouts, but I'd recommend either trimming it down to basics like a monday/wednesday/friday split of as many sets of 10 as you can with bodyweight squats/push ups/chin ups to keep it ruthlessly simple and easy to track progress - or - crossfit, where you've got a complex workout but you've got a trainer and a group of people to push you and keep you motivated.

glutes are built for lateral movement

Yeah glutes are a big part of your "hip drive". Your hips are a hinge, and your glutes, quads, and lower back all work together to straighten out the hinge. Thrusting your hips forward straightens out your body, if you can get used to using your tightening your core and using your glutes to straighten out the hip hinge, you're going to see huge improvements in squats, deadlifts, jumping, pretty much anything that requires your full body to push up.

I've always done one exercise at a time, and you start with the best most thorough compound exercise first, and then do lesser more complimentary exercises. This fatigues those muscles the most which is what a proper workout is. It is also helpful because you can really focus in on maintaining proper form all the way from your first exercise to the last.

I'd suggest prioritizing back squats. Back squats are the king of all lifts, though deadlifts are a close 2nd. That said, the other exercises seem redundant. Clearly you're trying to hit your lower body hard, it might be worth considering splitting the exercises to different days. Back squats and hip thrusts kind of go together because hip thrusts will hit your quads harder. Split squat hits your quads hard too and needs good balance. I know I would be an uncoordinated wobbly goof if I tried to do split squats after I did back squats. Glute bridge will work your hamstrings/glutes a little more. Monday/Thursday: back squat / hip thrust, Tuesday/Fridy: split-squat / glute bridge, on Wednesday/Saturday/Sunday you rest.

Just food for thought. As you get into it you will get a sense for what works. After a little while you'll notice the difference between "I feel weak because I'm not strong enough to do this", "I feel weak because I've not yet recovered from my previous workout", "I feel weak because I've already worked these muscles so hard this workout." The first feeling is the feeling that you should be pushing through and working hard, the second feeling is when you should not be be pushing yourself because you need to recover, the third feeling it's ok to push yourself hard to failure if you have recovery time planned before the next time that you work out.

Above all else I reccomend keeping a journal/log as you go through your work out. On every date list the exercise you did, how much weight, how many sets and how many reps. It may seem unimportant but as you do it you'll have questions about your progress or what exercises you've been doing and your log will be the only way you can answer them.
